question.text: In a double slit experiment with monochromatic light, fringes are obtained on a screen placed at some distance from the plane of slits. If the screen is moved by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> towards the slits, the change in fringe width is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the distance between the slits is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, then the wavelength of the light will be____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
We know that the fringe width in YDSE is β=λDd

⇒Δβ=λdΔD

⇒λ=ΔβdΔD=3×10-3×10-2×10-35×10-2=6×10-7 m=600 nm
